stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 1 < c < 8 \), for which \( g(c) = -8 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, such a c must exist, because g is differentiable on \( [1, 8] \), so it is continuous there, and \( g(1) = -9 < -8 < g(8) = 1 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable on \( [1, 8] \), so it is continuous there.
By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one such c.
